steps.one_line: Revisit file is 80.7 KB and diff-identical to step 11 except ids, one 'Also:' line and a FILE_ONLY revise block; the amend instruction never reaches the ~20 KB printed head. findings.quote: W1 has gone back to step-plan 1 of 2 times; this packet asks for an amended plan, not a new one. The result that sent it back (... the evidence to act on): RUN/results/nav-fbfb…
findings.evidence: These lines sit at offset 79,713 of 80,699 (packet line ~710), in the `deltas` block, which has tier FILE_ONLY in _producer_blocks. packet_head prints only P0/P1 plus whatever fits HEAD_LIMIT=20,000, and FILE_ONLY never prints. The head shows only the truncated status line 'Done: W1 implement (sent back to step-plan): The implement packet runs every suite:check command after every step.', which drops the real failure ('grep exits 2 because slChessBoard.html does not exist'), plus an 'Also:' line naming 'the previous step plan' with no path. _revise_delta_lines' own docstring says 'a model holding only this packet could not find the plan it is asked to amend'. The model got by only because the context was still warm: it opened results/nav-a3afbe… at 3218 s, 38 s after the callback.
findings.proposal: Move _revise_delta_lines out of the FILE_ONLY `deltas` block into _stage_input_blocks as a P1 block named 'revise', placed before 'step'. Also print the sent-back result's summary there, capped at 600 chars, so the failure itself is in the head.
findings.risk: None to obligations. This fixes a main-tenet violation: after a clear, the head alone must carry the revisit's input. To stay under HEAD_LIMIT, pay for it with C2-3 and C2-4.

findings.quote: The result that sent it back (accepted host report, untrusted; the evidence to act on)
findings.evidence: Implement's revise summary asked for a check that 'runs the C12 grep only when slChessBoard.html exists'. Step 17 adopted that literally (opening of step 18: 'Changed: the suite check... runs the C12 board grep only when slChessBoard.html exists'). That is a weaker stand-in', folded S1-S3 into one step, and spent 337 s doing it.
findings.proposal: Rewrite as: 'The result that sent it back (untrusted): <path>. Act on the failure it shows; its proposed fix is a suggestion, so adopt it only if every criterion's check still fails on a tree that lacks the criterion's work.'
findings.risk: Low. Improve still reviews the result. The line only saves a non-trivial Improve pass.

findings.quote: open it with a file tool, not the shell, when this print was cut (... === end ShipLoop head ===) or you need the duties or the template; it also holds the original request, the knowledge files quoted whole and the hand-offs.

cross_cutting.pattern: Revisit packets print the same head as the first visit. The only revisit-specific text is FILE_ONLY (deltas, last-accepted).
cross_cutting.evidence: diff 11 vs 17: only ids, one 'Also:' line, the narrative dropped, and the FILE_ONLY 'W1 has gone back...' block at offset 79,713. diff 13 vs 19 and 16 vs 22: only ids, plan text and quoted rows. _producer_blocks puts `last-accepted` and `deltas` in FILE_ONLY.
cross_cutting.proposal: A revisit packet should carry in P1, right after the status block: (1) why it is back, using the sent-back result's summary (≤600 chars) and path; (2) the previous accepted result of this same stage (path); (3) what changed upstream, as id-level adds, removes and changes computed by the script; (4) the rule 'keep untouched rows with their ids; the summary says what is carried over and what changed; a proposed fix in the evidence is a suggestion'. It can omit the knowledge quotes (path plus 'changed since last visit: <files>'). Keep the duties, rules, loop and template whole: they are the stage's own operating rules (main tenet).
cross_cutting.risk: Head grows ~1.2 KB on revisits. Pay for it with X3 and C2-4. The estimate counts the knowledge quotes dropped from 3 revisit files (~49 KB each).

cross_cutting.pattern: Only step-plan learns it is a revisit. test-spec, implement and their Improve handoffs do not.
cross_cutting.evidence: _sent_back_results returns None unless stage == stage_spec.REVISE_TO. 19 searched for its own prior spec (3794 s, 3807 s). 18, 20 and 23 handoffs have 0 hits for the previous-result ids. 20's reviewer used a model-made inbox copy.
cross_cutting.proposal: Make _sent_back_results(stage) return the previous accepted result of `stage` for any inner stage after the item's latest revise, and feed it to both _producer_blocks and improve_handoff_text.
cross_cutting.risk: Low. It adds locators and keeps all obligations.

cross_cutting.pattern: Stale pointer line: it says duties and template live only in the file.
cross_cutting.evidence: Packet line 7 in every producer packet. Duties and template have been P0 since 2026-10-16 (packet_head docstring).
cross_cutting.proposal: See C2-3: name what the file adds (knowledge, hand-offs, last accepted summary, request).
cross_cutting.risk: Update the packet-recut and packet-anatomy test regexes.

cross_cutting.pattern: Root cause of the whole revise loop (steps 16-21): the step-plan check guidance does not say checks run after every implement step.
cross_cutting.evidence: Step-plan duty 5 says 'check: the lint, type and build commands ... each safe to repeat locally.' Plan 11 made the whole-item C12 grep the only check. Implement 16 revised in 2 min ('On the S1 tree that grep exits 2'). The loop cost 16 (2.0) + 17 (9.5) + 19 (2.5) min of stage time, plus two Improve children (8.3 and 0.9 min) and a compaction.
cross_cutting.proposal: Append to duty 5's check bullet: 'Implement runs every check after every step, so each must exit 0 on S1's tree; a check that needs a later step's file means one step, or a per-step check in that step's criteria.'
cross_cutting.source: skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py step-plan duty 5 ('each safe to repeat locally')
cross_cutting.risk: None. It states a mechanic the gate already enforces. It would likely have saved ~14 min in this run.

cross_cutting.pattern: The quoted knowledge and test_cases are in packet files and handoffs that the model never opens, and they double in each Improve handoff.
cross_cutting.evidence: Quoted knowledge per file: 49.2 KB (17, 19), 29.5 KB (22). Handoffs: 76.3 KB (18), 79.7 KB (20), 98.0 KB (23), each requiring 'Read this whole file'. Implement quotes 14.5 KB of test_cases.
cross_cutting.proposal: Reference by path in revisit files (C2-9), in all Improve handoffs (C2-16) and for implement test_cases (C2-13).
cross_cutting.risk: The main tenet holds because each reference is a stable on-disk file named in the head. Estimate: 11 handoffs × ~45 KB plus 3 revisit files.

cross_cutting.evidence: Readers of the header 'ShipLoop navigator | <stage> | revision N': shiploop_status_hook.py HEADER (gate for the status hook), test/shiploop_e2e/clear.py HEADER, counters.py HEAD_START/HEADER, flow.py HEAD, metrics.py KEPT_REPLY/PACKET_STAGE, packet_anatomy.py, skills/shiploop-run-review/scripts/export.py, and template/index.html (first line starting 'ShipLoop navigator |'). The result heading '# ShipLoop navigator result' is not parsed: shiploop_store.loads reads only the shiploop-state fence. store.dumps writes it as the title of results/ records, and 10 tests assert it (e.g. test/shiploop-navigator-contract.test.py). The refusal prefix 'ShipLoop navigator: ' is written once at shiploop_protocol.py main (print(f"ShipLoop navigator: {exc}")), and test/shiploop_e2e/metrics.py counts failures by it (README §failures).
cross_cutting.proposal: Drop the template heading line from the Result template (safe; the model may write any heading). Shorten the header to 'ShipLoop | <stage> | rev N' and the refusal prefix to 'ShipLoop: ' only in one change that updates the 8 header readers and the metrics failure regex together. Saving is ~10-30 chars per packet, so do it for clarity, not size.
cross_cutting.risk: Breaking the status hook or E2E counters if readers are not changed in the same commit. Run-review older exports keep the old header, so readers would need to accept both forms for old runs, which conflicts with the one-supported-version rule. Accept only the new form and re-export.

cross_cutting.pattern: Code craft is printed whole (3.7 KB) despite owner rule 2.
cross_cutting.evidence: Lines 98-127 of 22 and '## Code craft' in the 23 handoff.
cross_cutting.risk: Verify the rule-9 composition cue survives as a one-liner.

Improve planning focus 'an expected result or check that a weaker stand-in would pass'. Review 18-1: 'the conditional check exits 0 when slChessBoard.html is absent ... That is a weaker stand-in', which restored the strict C12 grep.

Improve implement focus 'a language or library behaviour ... (comparison and case rules ...): run a one-line probe or read its primary documentation'. Review 23: 'String.equals is case-sensitive, so K and k stay distinct', plus a web search at 4848 s for AuraHandledException docs.

P1 'Prior Improve evidence and lessons' line in 19: it carried step 18's decision ('The suite check is the strict C12 grep. Do not skip that grep when slChessBoard.html is absent'), and 19 kept C12 strict without re-deciding.
Minimal Improve packet (1.9-2.7 KB). In 18, 20 and 23 every improve-pass and complete ran in order, with no refusal and no stray work.
Implement 'Check commands (run each after every edit ...)' with the exact grep printed. The model ran it at 4399 s and 4521 s, and the gate accepted on the first callback (4577 s).
